title: Withdrawing an Appeal — Unemployment Insurance Appeals Guidance Card
content:
Only the appellant may withdraw an appeal under Unemployment Insurance Appeals; the agent records the appellant's withdrawal request and the appeal is withdrawn once the appellant confirms it. An appeal may be withdrawn only while its status is filed or scheduled, that is, until the decision is issued. Withdrawal makes the appealed determination final as if no appeal had been filed: an overpayment's recovery resumes, and an appeal withdrawn after the filing deadline cannot be refiled.

## Who, what record, when

- **Who.** The appellant, and only the appellant. Another party to the appeal — the employer on a claimant's appeal, or the claimant on an employer's appeal — cannot withdraw it.
- **What the record must show.** A withdrawal request from the appellant recorded against that same appeal. The appeal is withdrawn once the appellant confirms that request; an unconfirmed request does not withdraw the appeal.
- **When.** While the appeal stands at filed or scheduled status — up to the issue of the decision.

| Status of the appeal | Withdrawal possible |
|---|---|
| filed | yes |
| scheduled | yes |
| decided | no (the decision has been issued) |
| dismissed | no |
| withdrawn | no (already withdrawn) |
| closed | no |

## Consequences of a withdrawal

| Consequence | Content |
|---|---|
| The appealed determination | becomes final as if no appeal had been filed |
| An appealed overpayment | its recovery resumes |
| Filing again | an appeal withdrawn after the filing deadline cannot be refiled |
| The appeal itself | stands withdrawn from the date the withdrawal was confirmed, and closes on that confirmation |

*Illustration (hypothetical):* a claimant withdraws an appeal of an overpayment determination while it stands scheduled, after the filing deadline for that determination has passed. Recovery of the overpayment resumes, and the claimant cannot file the appeal again.
